From \(a+b+c=0\) with \(|a|=|b|=|c|=1\), the angles \(x,y,z\) are separated by \(120^\circ\). Thus for some \(\theta\),

\[
\{x,y,z\}\equiv \{\theta,\theta+\tfrac{2\pi}{3},\theta+\tfrac{4\pi}{3}\}\pmod{2\pi}.
\]

Then

\[
y+z \equiv 3\theta - x \pmod{2\pi}.
\]

So

\[
2x-y-z \equiv 2x-(3\theta-x)=3(x-\theta)\pmod{2\pi}.
\]

Since \(x-\theta\) is one of \(0,\frac{2\pi}{3},\frac{4\pi}{3}\), we get

\[
2x-y-z \equiv 0 \pmod{2\pi}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\cos(2x-y-z)=1.
\]

The sum of all possible values is

\[
\boxed{1}.
\]
